articles.title: CoinShares Announces First Half 2026 Results - Positive Net Flows Despite A Sharp Digital Asset Market Decline; Strong Balance Sheet With $453 Million Of Net Assets And No Long-Term Debt
articles.description: CoinShares PLC (Nasdaq: CSHR) (“CoinShares” or the “Company”, together with its subsidiaries, the “Group”), a leading global asset manager specialising in digital assets, today announced its financial results for the six months ended June 30, 2026. First Half 2026 Highlights Total revenue of $51.4 million, compared with $80.0 million in H1 2025. Asset Management revenue was $40.0 million (H1 2025: $59.6 million), principally reflecting lower average Assets Under Management (“AUM”) following the decline in digital asset prices. Capital Markets revenue was $11.4 million (H1 2025: $22.1 million), with a further $3.4 million of gains from operations, resulting in Capital Markets Segment revenue and gains of $14.9 million (H1 2025: $26.5 million). Total AUM of $5.5 billion as of June 30, 2026, compared with $7.4 billion as of December 31, 2025. The decline in AUM was driven by market performance rather than net redemptions, with the Group generating $27.6 million of net inflows during the period. CoinShares Physical attracted $155.9 million of net inflows, partially offset at Group level by $104.6 million of net outflows from the legacy CoinShares XBT Provider platform. Operating loss was $5.1 million, compared with operating income of $75.9 million in H1 2025, while Segment EBITDA was $21.6 million, demonstrating continued underlying profitability despite the challenging market environment. Net loss was $23.9 million, including a $16.6 million unrealized loss arising from the XBT Pricing Differential and a $15.4 million unrealized loss on treasury digital asset holdings, together with one-time costs associated with the Nasdaq listing and settlement of a historic option plan. Strong balance sheet, with approximately $453 million of net assets, no long-term debt and an Available Capital Position of approximately $413.9 million, including approximately $284.6 million of earned and accrued CoinShares XBT management fees. The Board is seeking shareholder authority to establish a share repurchase program at the EGM scheduled for September 15, 2026, providing the Company with an additional capital allocation tool alongside continued investment in organic growth and selective acquisitions. Continued strategic progress across active alternative strategies, on-chain investment capabilities and the Group's regulated product range, including the expansion of staking products, progress following the acquisition of Bastion (completed in early September), development of initiatives with Kiln and Railnet, and the launch in July of the Company's first Bitcoin Mining UCITS ETF. Click here for full details.

articles.title: Promoting strategic ties with India is among PH foreign policy priorities
articles.description: Philippine-India relations are of vital strategic importance in 2026 because they provide a strong diplomatic and defense hedge against rising maritime tensions in the South China Sea while building secure technology supply chains through the US-led Pax Silica coalition. It is in this context that the current visit to India of President Ferdinand R. Marcos, Jr. must be viewed. He is joining other regional leaders, such as Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim and Vietnamese Prime Minister Le Minh Hung, whose countries are BRICS partners. BRICS is the coalition formed by Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa to promote strategic alliances that is now marking its 20th year. Presenting the imperatives guiding ASEAN is also part of President Marcos’ agenda in view of the Philippines’ chairship at the forthcoming summit in Manila this November. “We will call for fairer global governance, stronger disaster preparedness, and the responsible use of new technologies, climate action, and the peaceful settlement of disputes under international law,” the President said. He will also share lessons from ASEAN’s long-standing commitment to an open and inclusive dialogue while preserving the region’s strategic autonomy. Apart from the summit, President Marcos will meet with Prime Minister Modi to review progress in key areas of the Philippines-India Strategic Partnership, a year after the President’s state visit to India. Last year, Philippines-India relations were elevated to a strategic partnership that has since witnessed top-level defense strategy talks and increased official and business exchanges in areas such as financial technology, agriculture, and tourism. Both the Philippines and India face security pressures from China’s assertive actions in their respective regions. New Delhi worries about stability in the South China Sea because vital Indian trade passes through these waters. Manila and New Delhi are deepening military ties, highlighted by the acquisition of India’s BrahMos supersonic anti-ship missile system by the Philippine military. Forward pathways to be pursued by both countries in Pax Silica are also ripe for discussion. The partnership connects the Philippines' planned AI-native industrial hub in New Clark City with India’s massive technology and software talent pool. Over 20 Indian AI and advanced manufacturing firms are exploring investments in the Philippines under this tech framework. Economic and supply chain diversification would enable both countries to diversify their economic and diplomatic ties while avoiding over-dependence on any single global superpower. Beyond defense and microchips, bilateral discussions focus on pharmaceuticals, digital innovation, direct air connectivity, and a preferential trade agreement that involves Further down the road, the Philippines and India are working towards finalizing a Preferential Trade Agreement (PTA) that would involve launching direct air connectivity, and implementing reciprocal visa-free travel and e-visa initiatives. Plans are underway to establish direct flight routes connecting major hubs like Manila and New Delhi. Also on tap is the implementation of simplified travel frameworks, including visa-free travel for Indian nationals visiting the Philippines, and, conversely, free e-visas for Filipinos traveling to India. Indeed, taking the opportunity to assess and accelerate the pace of bilateral cooperation would bode well for strengthening the Philippines-India alliance while enhancing mutual respect and cooperation. It also reinforces the Philippines’ ASEAN chairship and provides expanded global recognition that will serve the country in good stead for decades to come.
